mainTopic: When a תודה needs its לחם: רבי יוחנן's rulings on replacements and offspring, שמואל's comparison to the חטאת, and how a תודה relates to its לחם.
overview: A letter from רב חנינא quoted רבי יוחנן: one kind of תודה needs לחם if it is brought before the owner's כפרה, but not after. The גמרא rules out the replacement of a voluntary תודה and the offspring of a voluntary תודה. It settles on the offspring of an obligatory תודה. The lesson is that אדם מתכפר בשבח הקדש, and an explicit statement of רבי יוחנן confirms all three rules. Next, שמואל ties the לחם of a תודה to whether a חטאת in the same situation dies or grazes. After challenges from רב עמרם and others, the גמרא concludes that שמואל follows רבי שמעון and said only the 'dies' half of the rule. In doing so he rejects רבי יוחנן's idea of gaining כפרה through שבח הקדש. Finally, רבי אבא teaches that lost לחם is replaced but a lost תודה is not, because the לחם exists for the תודה. רבא then begins a case about money set aside for a תודה, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Could he mean the replacement of a voluntary thanks offering? No.
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רבי יוחנן meant the חליפין of a תודה נדבה, and rejects it, since that replacement always needs לחם.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, maybe he meant the replacement of a voluntary thanks offering? That can't be: whether before atonement or after atonement, they need loaves, because he is simply adding more thanks offerings!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a new guess at what case רבי יוחנן was talking about, and right away shows that the guess doesn't fit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a נדבה, the owner never had to replace a lost animal, so a replacement counts as an extra voluntary תודה. A voluntary תודה always needs לחם, before or after כפרה. That clashes with רבי יוחנן's 'before yes, after no' ruling, so this case is ruled out.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; it introduces a new suggestion after the last one failed
A replacement animal, brought when the first one was lost
Thanks offering, which normally comes with loaves of bread
A voluntary offering: 'this animal is a תודה.' If it is lost, the owner does not have to replace it.
Atonement; here, the moment the owner's offering is brought and he has fulfilled it
Adding more thanks offerings, so each one counts as its own תודה with its own לחם

phrases.english: Rather, [perhaps he meant] the replacement of a voluntary thanks offering
whether before atonement
or after atonement
they require loaves
he is one who increases thanks offerings!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the search for the case in רבי יוחנן's letter, after the replacement of an obligatory תודה was rejected earlier.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects reading רבי יוחנן's ruling as being about a replacement for a voluntary תודה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: That replacement needs לחם both before and after כפרה, so it can't be the case where the timing makes a difference.

steps.title: Could he mean the offspring of a voluntary thanks offering? No.
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the ולד of a תודה נדבה, and rejects it, since that offspring never needs לחם.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, maybe he meant the offspring of a voluntary thanks offering? That can't be: whether before atonement or after atonement, it doesn't need loaves, because it is a leftover of the thanks offering!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a second guess, the baby animal born to a voluntary תודה, and rejects that one too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ולד of a תודה counts as a מותר, an extra that comes from the תודה, and an extra never needs לחם. Since its rule is the same before and after כפרה, it can't be רבי יוחנן's case.

keyTerms.meaning: Offspring, an animal born to a sanctified mother
Leftover or extra of a sacrifice; it does not get its own לחם

phrases.english: Rather, [perhaps he meant] the offspring of a voluntary thanks offering

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין לִפְנֵי כַפָּרָה בֵּין לְאַחַר כַּפָּרָה
phrases.english: whether before atonement or after atonement
they do not require loaves
it is a leftover of the thanks offering!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the replacement of a voluntary תודה failed, the גמרא tries the offspring of a voluntary תודה.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects reading the ruling as being about the ולד of a voluntary תודה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: That offspring never needs לחם, so the before-or-after difference doesn't apply to it.

steps.title: He meant the offspring of an obligatory thanks offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא settles on the ולד of a תודה חובה: before כפרה it needs לחם, and after כפרה it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he meant the offspring of an obligatory thanks offering: before atonement it needs loaves, and after atonement it doesn't need loaves.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finally finds a case that fits רבי יוחנן's ruling: the baby animal of a תודה the owner was obligated to bring.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a חובה, the owner still owes a תודה until he brings one. If he brings the ולד before its mother, the ולד can count as his offering, so it needs לחם. Once the mother has already been brought and he has his כפרה, the ולד is just a leftover and needs no לחם.

keyTerms.meaning: An obligatory offering: 'I take upon myself a תודה.' The owner stays responsible until he brings one.
Requires the loaves that come with a תודה

steps.whatToRemember: The only case where 'before כפרה needs לחם, after כפרה doesn't' works is the ולד of an obligatory תודה.

phrases.english: Rather, [he meant] the offspring of an obligatory thanks offering
before atonement it requires loaves
after atonement it does not require loaves.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After two failed guesses, this third suggestion is accepted.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies the specific case behind the ruling
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ruling could have been about a replacement, or about the offspring of a voluntary תודה.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is about the ולד of an obligatory תודה, where the timing of the כפרה decides whether it needs לחם.

steps.title: What is the new lesson here?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי יוחנן's ruling, read this way, is teaching us.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is this teaching us?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that the case is known, the גמרא asks what new idea it teaches. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once a ruling is placed in a specific case, the גמרא wants to know what principle makes it worth saying. The answer comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it teaching us? The גמרא uses this to ask for the new point of a ruling.

phrases.english: What is he teaching us?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the principle behind the case that was just accepted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The principle that the ruling about an obligatory תודה's offspring teaches.

steps.title: A person can gain atonement through the growth of a sanctified animal
steps.stepSummary: The lesson is that רבי יוחנן holds אדם מתכפר בשבח הקדש: the ולד of the sanctified animal can serve as the owner's own offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: That רבי יוחנן holds: a person can gain atonement through the growth of sanctified property.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ruling teaches a principle: the offspring, which 'grew out of' the sanctified animal, can count as the owner's offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might think only the animal the owner actually set aside can fulfill his obligation. רבי יוחנן holds that its offspring, a שבח (growth) of the הקדש, can also bring him כפרה. That is why the ולד brought before its mother needs לחם.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds, as a matter of opinion
Gains atonement, meaning his offering is fulfilled through it
The growth or added value of sanctified property, such as an offspring

steps.whyThisMatters: This principle is what makes the timing matter. Before כפרה, the ולד can be the actual offering. After כפרה, it is only an extra.

phrases.english: That Rabbi Yoḥanan holds:
a person achieves atonement with the enhancement of consecrated property.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question in step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יוחנן holds אדם מתכפר בשבח הקדש, so the ולד of an obligatory תודה can serve as the offering itself.

steps.title: אביי analyzed the letter the same way
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that אביי also worked through רב חנינא's letter and reached the same conclusions.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי also discussed it in this same way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a short note that another great sage, אביי, explained the letter just like this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This adds no new reasoning. It shows that the analysis just given is shared by אביי, which makes it stronger.

keyTerms.meaning: He discussed it, working through the matter
In this same way

phrases.english: Abaye also discussed it
in this way.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָוֵי בַּהּ נָמֵי אַבָּיֵי כִּי הַאי גַוְונָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds that אביי agrees with the analysis just completed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אביי's reading of the letter matches the one just given.

steps.title: An explicit statement of רבי יוחנן confirms all three rulings
steps.stepSummary: רב יצחק בר יוסף reports רבי יוחנן saying outright what the analysis worked out. A voluntary replacement always needs לחם. A voluntary offspring never does. An obligatory offspring needs לחם only before כפרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also stated: רב יצחק בר יוסף said in the name of רבי יוחנן: the replacement of a voluntary thanks offering, before or after atonement, needs loaves, because he is adding more thanks offerings. The offspring of a voluntary thanks offering, before or after atonement, doesn't need loaves, because it is a leftover of the thanks offering. The offspring of an obligatory thanks offering needs loaves before atonement, and doesn't need loaves after atonement.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a direct quote from רבי יוחנן that spells out exactly the three rules worked out above.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now, the conclusions came from reasoning about which case fits the letter. This statement shows רבי יוחנן actually said all three rules himself, so the analysis is confirmed.

keyTerms.meaning: Replacement of a voluntary thanks offering; it always needs לחם
Offspring of a voluntary thanks offering; it never needs לחם
Offspring of an obligatory thanks offering; it needs לחם only before כפרה

steps.whatToRemember: Three rules: (1) a voluntary replacement always needs לחם; (2) a voluntary offspring never needs לחם; (3) an obligatory offspring needs לחם before כפרה but not after.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up 'replacement' and 'offspring.' A replacement is a new animal brought in place of a lost one. An offspring is born from the sanctified animal itself.

phrases.english: It was also stated:
Rav Yitzḥak bar Yosef says
that Rabbi Yoḥanan says:
The replacement of a voluntary thanks offering

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין לִפְנֵי כַפָּרָה בֵּין לְאַחַר כַּפָּרָה –
phrases.english: whether before atonement or after atonement
requires loaves
he is one who increases thanks offerings.
The offspring of a voluntary thanks offering

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין לִפְנֵי כַפָּרָה בֵּין לְאַחַר כַּפָּרָה –
phrases.english: whether before atonement or after atonement
does not require loaves
it is a leftover of the thanks offering.
And the offspring of an obligatory thanks offering
before atonement requires loaves
after atonement does not require loaves.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר נָמֵי, אָמַר רַב יִצְחָק בַּר יוֹסֵף, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the analysis of steps 1 to 6 with an explicit statement.
steps.raayaObject: The three rulings reached by working out which case רבי יוחנן's letter meant.
steps.raayaSupportSource: An explicit statement of רבי יוחנן, reported by רב יצחק בר יוסף.

steps.title: שמואל's rule linking sin offering and thanks offering
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that the fate of a leftover חטאת tells us whether a leftover תודה needs לחם. If the חטאת dies, the תודה needs no לחם. If the חטאת grazes, the תודה needs לחם.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: whenever a חטאת in some situation is left to die, a תודה in that same situation does not need bread. Whenever a חטאת in some situation is sent to graze, a תודה in that same situation does need bread.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new general rule from שמואל that compares two kinds of קרבנות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A leftover חטאת has one of two outcomes. Either it is locked away to die (מתה), or it grazes until it gets a blemish and is then sold (רועה). שמואל says this tells us whether a leftover תודה brings its לחם. 'Dies' means no לחם, and 'grazes' means it needs לחם.

keyTerms.meaning: A sin offering that cannot be used and is left to die
A sin offering sent to graze until it gets a blemish, then sold
Requires the accompanying loaves

steps.whyThisMatters: This rule gives one simple test for all the לחם questions about lost and replaced תודות in this sugya.

phrases.english: Shmuel says:
Any case where, with a sin offering, it is left to die,
with a thanks offering it does not require bread.
Any case where, with a sin offering, it grazes,
with a thanks offering it requires bread.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the analysis of רבי יוחנן's rulings, the גמרא brings a new general rule about לחם for a replaced תודה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A תודה needs לחם exactly when a חטאת in the same situation would graze, and needs none when the חטאת would die.

steps.title: רב עמרם cites the ברייתא on a lost and found thanks offering
steps.stepSummary: רב עמרם begins his challenge by quoting a ברייתא. When a lost תודה is found after a replacement was set aside, he offers either one with לחם, and the other needs no לחם.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב עמרם objected. What does the פסוק 'he shall offer the thanks offering' teach? Someone set aside a תודה, it got lost, and he set aside another in its place. Then the first was found, so now both are standing. How do we know he may offer whichever one he wants, with its bread? The פסוק says 'he shall offer the thanks offering.' Might the second one also need bread? The פסוק says 'he shall offer it': one, not two.
steps.whatsHappening: רב עמרם starts an objection to שמואל by quoting a ברייתא about a תודה. This step sets up the challenge, and the next step completes it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this case the first animal was found before he got his כפרה, and the second animal needs no לחם. By שמואל's rule, a חטאת in the same case should be left to die. The next step checks whether that is true.

keyTerms.meaning: One who sets aside an animal as a קרבן
It was lost
The פסוק teaches
One might have thought

phrases.english: Rav Amram raises an objection:
What is it teaching when it says: "He shall offer the thanks offering"?
From where do we know, for one who separates his thanks offering and it was lost,
and he separated another in its place,
and the first was found,
and now both of them are standing:
from where do we know that whichever of them he wishes
he may offer, with its bread along with it?
The verse teaches: "He shall offer the thanks offering."
One might think the second one also requires bread?
The verse teaches: "He shall offer it":
one, and not two.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This begins an objection to שמואל's rule from step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's rule that a תודה needs no לחם only where a חטאת would die
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A תודה found before כפרה needs no לחם for the second animal. So by שמואל's rule the parallel חטאת should die. The next step shows it actually grazes according to the חכמים.

steps.title: In the same case a sin offering grazes
steps.stepSummary: רב עמרם completes the challenge. In the matching חטאת case, the חכמים say that if the animal was found before the owner's כפרה, it grazes. That breaks שמואל's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: But with a חטאת in this same kind of case, the animal grazes. As we learned in a משנה: someone set aside his חטאת, it got lost, and he set aside another in its place. Then the first was found, so now both are standing. He gets his כפרה with one of them, and the second must die; these are the words of רבי. The חכמים say a חטאת is left to die only if it was found after the owner got his כפרה. That means if it was found before the owner got his כפרה, it grazes.
steps.whatsHappening: רב עמרם finishes his objection. He shows that in the same case, a חטאת grazes, yet the תודה still needs no לחם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the חכמים, a חטאת found before כפרה grazes. By שמואל's rule, the matching תודה should then need לחם. But the ברייתא says the second תודה needs no לחם. So שמואל's rule seems to fail.

keyTerms.meaning: Gains atonement through the קרבן
The owner of the קרבן
It follows that (an inference from the wording)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two views. רבי says the second חטאת always dies. Only the חכמים say it grazes if found before כפרה, and the challenge is built on the חכמים.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִילּוּ גַּבֵּי חַטָּאת כִּי הַאי גַּוְנָא רוֹעָה,
phrases.english: Whereas regarding a sin offering in a case like this, it grazes,
as we learned in a משנה:
If he separated his sin offering and it was lost,
and he separated another in its place,
and the first was found,
and now both of them are standing:
he gains atonement with one of them
and the second shall die; these are the words of Rabbi.
And the Sages say:
A sin offering is not left to die except
when it was found after the owner gained atonement;
so if it was found before the owner gained atonement, it grazes.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִילּוּ גַּבֵּי חַטָּאת כִּי הַאי גַּוְנָא רוֹעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This completes רב עמרם's objection that began in step 9.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to the חכמים, a חטאת found before כפרה grazes. So by שמואל the תודה should need לחם, but the ברייתא says the second תודה does not.

steps.title: שמואל follows רבי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that שמואל follows רבי. In רבי's view, a חטאת that was lost when its replacement was set aside is left to die, so the rule fits the ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל holds like רבי, who said: an animal that was lost at the time the replacement was set aside is left to die.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רב עמרם by saying שמואל holds like רבי, not like the חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי, what matters is that the first animal was lost when the replacement was set aside. Such a חטאת dies even if it is found before כפרה. So the חטאת dies, the תודה needs no לחם, and שמואל's rule matches the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds (this opinion)
Lost at the time the replacement was set aside

steps.whatToRemember: This answer solves רב עמרם's challenge for now. The גמרא tests it again in step 12 and, in step 15, drops it: שמואל is said to follow רבי שמעון instead.

phrases.english: Shmuel holds in accordance with Rabbi,
who said:
one that was lost at the time of separation is left to die.
phrases.notes: He means: even if it turns up before the owner gets his כפרה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This answers רב עמרם's objection from steps 9-10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the אמורא to one side of a תנאים dispute
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל's rule seemed to follow the חכמים, under whom a חטאת found before כפרה grazes.
steps.terutzMaskana: שמואל follows רבי, under whom a חטאת lost at the time of separation dies, so the matching תודה needs no לחם.

steps.title: When does a חטאת ever graze according to רבי?
steps.stepSummary: If רבי says a lost חטאת dies, the גמרא asks where רבי would ever send a חטאת out to graze.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if so, how can you find a case of grazing according to רבי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא just said שמואל follows רבי, who lets the lost חטאת die. Now it asks where a 'grazing' חטאת would ever happen for רבי, because שמואל's second rule talks about grazing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל's rule had two halves: 'dies' means no לחם, and 'grazes' means לחם. If רבי sends the lost-and-found חטאת to die, the גמרא needs a case where רבי says a חטאת grazes. Otherwise the second half of שמואל's rule would have nothing to apply to.

keyTerms.meaning: Grazes: the animal is put out to pasture until it gets a blemish, then sold
How can you find it? A request for a real case

phrases.english: But grazing, according to Rabbi —
how can you find it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא רוֹעָה, לְרַבִּי הֵיכִי מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the answer of Step 11 by asking how the 'grazing' half of שמואל's rule fits רבי.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A case where רבי rules that a חטאת is sent to graze.

steps.title: רבי אושעיא's case of two backup חטאות
steps.stepSummary: Grazing happens when someone sets aside two חטאות as a backup. He brings one, and the other grazes.
steps.simpleTranslation: Like רבי אושעיא's case. רבי אושעיא said: if a person set aside two חטאות as a backup, he gets his כפרה with whichever one he wants, and the second one grazes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a grazing case that even רבי agrees to. Someone set aside two חטאות on purpose so he would have a spare, and the spare goes out to graze.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here no animal was ever lost. The extra one was set aside on purpose as insurance. Since it was never a 'lost' animal, even רבי does not make it die. It grazes instead.

keyTerms.meaning: As a guarantee or backup, in case the first animal gets lost

phrases.english: Like Rabbi Oshaya's case,
for Rabbi Oshaya said:
If one set aside two sin offerings as a guarantee,
he gains atonement with whichever of them he wants,
and the second shall graze.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 12 with a concrete grazing case.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The case of two חטאות set aside as a backup: the leftover one grazes, even according to רבי.

steps.title: In that same case a תודה needs no לחם
steps.stepSummary: When a backup תודה is left over in the same kind of case, it needs no לחם. That breaks 'grazes means לחם'.
steps.simpleTranslation: But with a תודה, in a case like this, it does not need לחם!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks again. In the backup case the חטאת grazes, yet a backup תודה in the same situation does not need לחם. So שמואל's 'grazing means לחם' rule does not work under רבי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The only grazing case רבי has is the backup case. In that exact case the extra תודה brings no לחם. So if שמואל followed רבי, his second rule would give the wrong answer.

keyTerms.meaning: In a case like this one
It does not need the loaves that normally come with a תודה

phrases.english: But regarding a thanks offering,
in a case like this,
it does not require loaves!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא גַּבֵּי תוֹדָה כִּי הַאי גַוְונָא אֵין טְעוּנָה לֶחֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the answer of Step 13 to show that שמואל cannot follow רבי.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim (Step 11) that שמואל follows רבי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under רבי the only grazing case is the backup case. A backup תודה needs no לחם, which contradicts שמואל's 'grazes means לחם'.

steps.title: שמואל follows רבי שמעון instead
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא switches: שמואל holds like רבי שמעון, who lists five חטאות that die, including the backup one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, שמואל holds like רבי שמעון, who said: five חטאות die.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops רבי and says שמואל follows רבי שמעון. רבי שמעון says the backup חטאת dies, which matches the backup תודה needing no לחם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי שמעון, the backup case is a 'dying' case. That lines up with שמואל's first rule: dies means no לחם. So the backup case no longer contradicts שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: Five kinds of חטאת that are left to die and cannot be used

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא שְׁמוּאֵל כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן סְבִירָא לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: Rather, Shmuel holds like Rabbi Shimon,
who said: five sin offerings die.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא שְׁמוּאֵל כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן סְבִירָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 14 by replacing רבי with רבי שמעון as שמואל's source.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigning שמואל to a different תנא
steps.terutzMaskana: שמואל follows רבי שמעון, for whom the backup חטאת dies, so the backup תודה rightly needs no לחם.

steps.title: רבי שמעון has no grazing at all
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון never sends a חטאת to graze, so שמואל's 'grazing' rule would have nothing to talk about.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבי שמעון does not have grazing at all!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the new answer. If שמואל follows רבי שמעון, his 'grazes means לחם' rule is empty, because רבי שמעון has no grazing case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The switch to רבי שמעון fixed the backup case but created a new problem. רבי שמעון makes every leftover חטאת die. So why would שמואל make a rule about grazing?

keyTerms.meaning: He does not hold of it at all

phrases.english: But grazing —
Rabbi Shimon does not hold of it at all!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא רוֹעָה, לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן לֵית לֵיהּ כְּלָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that שמואל follows רבי שמעון.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל's second rule speaks about grazing, but רבי שמעון has no grazing case, so the rule would be pointless.

steps.title: שמואל said only one rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that שמואל only said: whatever makes a חטאת die makes a תודה need no לחם.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל also only said one thing: any case where a חטאת dies, a תודה in that case does not need לחם.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by trimming שמואל's statement. He never said the 'grazing' half. He only said the 'dying' half.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the grazing rule is removed, following רבי שמעון causes no trouble. שמואל's rule only covers dying cases, and רבי שמעון has plenty of those.

keyTerms.meaning: He said only one thing
Dies: the animal is left alone until it dies and cannot be used

steps.confusionAlert: Step 8 showed שמואל with two rules. Here the גמרא concludes he really said only the first one, about a חטאת that dies.
steps.whatToRemember: Final version of שמואל: if a חטאת would die in a certain case, a תודה in that same case needs no לחם. There is no rule about grazing.

phrases.english: Shmuel too said only one thing:
any case where with a sin offering it dies —
with a thanks offering it does not require loaves.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 16 by correcting what שמואל actually said.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Correcting the wording of the statement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל said two rules, one for dying and one for grazing.
steps.terutzMaskana: שמואל said only the dying rule, which fits רבי שמעון.

steps.title: What is שמואל's point?
steps.stepSummary: With only one rule left, the גמרא asks what new lesson שמואל is teaching.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is he teaching us?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what we gain from שמואל's single rule. This sets up the next step, which explains who he is arguing against.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי שמעון already says which חטאות die, matching the תודה to them might seem obvious. The גמרא wants to know what extra point שמואל is making.

keyTerms.meaning: What is he teaching us? A request for the new point

phrases.english: What is he teaching us?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the purpose of the corrected rule from Step 17.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The new point in שמואל's single rule.

steps.title: Rejecting רבי יוחנן's 'added value of הקדש'
steps.stepSummary: שמואל comes to argue with רבי יוחנן, who says a person can gain כפרה through the added value of הקדש. שמואל says no.
steps.simpleTranslation: To reject the view of רבי יוחנן, who said: a person gains כפרה through the added value of הקדש. שמואל teaches us that he does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that שמואל is arguing with רבי יוחנן. רבי יוחנן says a person can use the 'extra' that grew from his offering, such as its offspring, for his כפרה. שמואל disagrees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 7 said that, according to רבי יוחנן, an obligatory תודה's offspring needs לחם before כפרה, because the owner can use it for his obligation. שמואל ties the offspring to the חטאת rule. An offspring of a חטאת dies, so an offspring of a תודה needs no לחם, since you cannot gain כפרה through the added value of הקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: To exclude, meaning to reject another opinion
The added value of הקדש, like an offspring born from a consecrated animal
He teaches us

steps.whyThisMatters: This makes שמואל and רבי יוחנן disagree about the offspring of an obligatory תודה brought before כפרה. רבי יוחנן requires לחם, and שמואל does not.

phrases.english: To exclude the view of Rabbi Yoḥanan,
who said: a person gains atonement through the added value of consecrated property,
phrases.notes: The 'added value' here means something like the offspring of the consecrated animal.

phrases.english: he teaches us that he does not.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 18 by naming the view שמואל rejects.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: שמואל rejects רבי יוחנן's view that a person gains כפרה through the added value of הקדש. So a תודה's offspring needs no לחם, just as a חטאת's offspring dies.

steps.title: Lost loaves are replaced, a lost thanks offering is not
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא rules that if the לחם set aside for a תודה is lost, new לחם is brought. If the תודה animal itself is lost, no new תודה is brought.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא says: If someone said 'this is a תודה and this is its לחם': if the לחם was lost, he brings other לחם. If the תודה was lost, he does not bring another תודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. רבי אבא gives a rule about a person who set aside both a תודה animal and the material for its loaves, and then lost one of them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two cases are not treated the same. Losing the לחם does not cancel the offering: you just replace the לחם. But losing the תודה ends the whole thing, and he does not have to bring a new animal.

keyTerms.meaning: Its bread: the loaves that go with the תודה
Was lost
Another, a replacement

steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume the two halves are a mirror image. Only the לחם gets replaced. A lost תודה is not replaced at all.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba says:
This is a thanks offering and this is its bread,
if the bread was lost, he brings other bread;

phrases.aramaic: אָבְדָה תּוֹדָה – אֵינוֹ מֵבִיא תּוֹדָה אַחֶרֶת.
phrases.english: if the thanks offering was lost, he does not bring another thanks offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא: זוֹ תּוֹדָה וְזוֹ לַחְמָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the שמואל and רבי יוחנן discussion and opens a new teaching about the תודה and its לחם.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Lost לחם is replaced. A lost תודה is not replaced.

steps.title: Asking for the reason behind the difference
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the לחם is replaced but the תודה is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind רבי אבא's rule. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not an attack on רבי אבא. The גמרא only wants to understand why the two lost items are treated differently.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind רבי אבא's rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why lost לחם is replaced but a lost תודה is not.

steps.title: The loaves exist for the thanks offering, not the reverse
steps.stepSummary: The לחם comes because of the תודה, but the תודה does not come because of the לחם.
steps.simpleTranslation: The לחם is on account of the תודה, but the תודה is not on account of the לחם.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the תודה is the main item and the לחם is only an add-on that serves it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the main item, the תודה, is gone, the add-on has no reason to be brought, so nothing is replaced. If the add-on, the לחם, is gone, the main offering still stands, so he just brings new לחם.

keyTerms.meaning: On account of, because of

steps.whatToRemember: The תודה is the main item and the לחם depends on it. Lose the לחם and you replace it. Lose the תודה and there is nothing for new לחם to serve.

phrases.english: The bread is on account of the thanks offering,
but the thanks offering is not on account of the bread.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֶחֶם לִגְלַל תּוֹדָה, וְאֵין תּוֹדָה לִגְלַל לֶחֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The לחם depends on the תודה, so only the לחם can be replaced on its own.

steps.title: רבא begins a rule about money set aside for a thanks offering
steps.stepSummary: רבא opens a new case: someone who set aside money for his תודה. His ruling continues in the next section.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: If someone set aside money for his תודה...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move. רבא begins a new case about money set aside for a תודה, and his actual ruling comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, the case was an actual animal and actual loaves. Now the case is money that was set aside to buy the תודה. The ruling about how the תודה and לחם relate in this case has not been given yet.

keyTerms.meaning: Set aside, designated
Money, coins
For his thanks offering

phrases.english: And Rava said:
If one set aside money for his thanks offering
phrases.notes: The sentence isn't finished yet. רבא's ruling continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another teaching on the same subject of the תודה and its לחם, this time about money set aside for them.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Setup only. The case of money set aside for a תודה is introduced, and the ruling follows in the next section.
